_readme: Featured Projects source of truth. GENERATED SURFACES stamped from this file
by scripts/build-projects.mjs: docs/our-work.html (OURWORK-STATIC +
OURWORK-HEAD-SCHEMA regions), the OURWORK-STRIP 'Recent jobs' regions on the
/services/ hub pages, and docs/assets/data/homeowner-wall.json. Edit here,
then run: node scripts/build-projects.mjs — and commit ALL stamped files.
Publish procedure + field rules: documentation/runbooks/PUBLISH-PROJECT.md
TAXONOMY: services[] is required — 1+ of roof-replacement|roof-repair|
siding-replacement|siding-repair|wood-siding-repair|shed-roof-replacement|
gutter-replacement|storm-damage|
roof-inspection (the /services/ hub filenames). It drives the /our-work
filter buttons, #service= deep links, schema serviceType, the card pills,
and which hub-page strips a job appears in. category is legacy/optional.
SORTING: surfaces render newest published first — APPEND new entries at the
END of this array; same-date entries keep array order.
HARD RULES: retail prices only (priceLow/priceHigh, both or neither, whole
dollars) — never cost/margin figures; city-level location only, never a real
location; photos must be re-encoded copies under /assets/images/projects/
(the re-encode strips EXIF), never CRM storage URLs; consentOnFile must be
true or the build refuses the entry; a future published date stages the
entry until the first deploy after that date.
OPTIONAL CASE-STUDY FIELDS (2026-09-27): problem, scope, materials, timeline,
outcome — each renders its own H2 (The problem / What we did / Materials /
Timeline / Result) on /our-work/<slug> ONLY when present; scope and materials
may be a list of strings. Photos may carry an optional caption (falls back to
alt). Write only what is true of the job — the template never fills a gap.
city ('Town, ST') also places the job on /areas/<town> and the town-specific
/services/<service>-<town> pages (OURWORK-AREA / OURWORK-LOCAL regions).

projects.title: Brick Colonial — Full Re-Roof
projects.description: Architectural shingle replacement on a two-story colonial. New drip edge, starter strip, and ridge vent. Curb appeal speaks for itself.

photos.alt: Completed roof on brick colonial home with spring landscaping
Elevated drone view of the finished colonial, fresh shingle planes over the brick front and attached garage
Rooftop-level view across the garage wing of the same colonial, clean new shingle courses in spring sun

projects.title: Brick Two-Story — Drone Verified
projects.description: Complete tear-off and replacement. Every project gets drone documentation so the homeowner can see exactly what was done — and so can the insurance company.

photos.alt: Aerial drone view of completed brick home roof replacement
Overhead drone view of the finished brick two-story, chimney and full roof plane in frame
Wider overhead of the same brick home showing the rear patio, garage wing and complete new roof

projects.title: Multi-Section Complex Roof
projects.description: A large brick two-story with multiple roof sections, valleys and wall transitions, its old shingles faded and streaked on every plane. The crew tore off every section, dried the whole roof in under synthetic underlayment, then laid new architectural shingles with all flashing replaced: new step and counter flashing at the brick walls, new pipe boots and a new ridge vent. Before, install day and the finished roof are all in the photos.

photos.alt: Wide overhead of the same roof before the work, shingles faded and streaked across every plane
Low-angle eave detail before the work showing deteriorated decking behind the gutter line
Five crew members mid tear-off across three roof sections as old shingles come off
Tear-off complete on the garage wing with bare decking exposed and underlayment going down
Wide aerial of the job site with the crew spread across the felt-covered roof and trucks staged below
Crew rolling out synthetic underlayment across the main roof plane with shingle bundles staged along the ridge
Underlayment-covered plane with a roofer detailing the brick chimney and shingle bundles nearby
Complex multi-section roof replacement completed
Tight aerial of the finished work with new architectural shingle across the complex hip roof
Finished detail: crisp valley lines, ridge cap and new pipe boots on the fresh shingle plane
Low-angle view of a finished lower roof section against the brick wall with new step and counter flashing
Finished main roof plane with new pipe boots and the rebuilt chimney with its new caps
Close detail of the finished hip and ridge vent run on the completed roof

projects.title: Wind Damage — Lifted & Missing Shingles
projects.description: High winds peeled back shingles and exposed underlayment. Documented damage for insurance claim, full replacement approved and completed within two weeks.

photos.alt: Storm damaged roof with lifted and missing shingles
The same wind-damaged roof with an emergency tarp cap-nailed over the exposed ridge
The completed replacement roof in fresh gray shingles with a new ridge vent run

projects.title: Hail Impact — Chalk-Marked Inspection
projects.description: I mark every impact with chalk during inspection so the adjuster can verify. This roof had 50+ hits per test square — clear approval for full replacement.

photos.alt: Chalk-marked hail damage during roof inspection
Ridge view of the hail-inspected roof showing a box vent, pipe boot and chalk-marked impact
Straight-down close-up of chalk-circled hail hits across the brown shingle field

projects.title: Full Crew — Cul-de-Sac Tear-Off
projects.description: Branded trucks, tarps down, materials staged, crew on the roof. This is what a professional jobsite looks like. Neighbors took notice — two more estimates booked that week.

photos.alt: NBD crew actively working on roof tear-off in residential neighborhood
High aerial over the backyard toward the cul-de-sac with the crew working on exposed decking mid tear-off
Overview of the whole property and cul-de-sac with the ridge torn off to bare decking
Afternoon progress: synthetic underlayment across the upper slopes with new shingle courses starting
Detail down the main slope with underlayment laid and shingle bundles staged for the install
Three-quarter aerial of the completed roof in morning sun, new designer-blend shingles on every plane
Top-down finished detail showing full shingle texture, a straight ridge line and clean valleys
Low-angle side elevation of the finished roofline across all planes, chimney and vents in place

projects.title: Valley Flashing Detail — Precision Install
projects.description: Metal valley flashing with tight shingle cuts on both sides, new pipe boot sealed properly. This is the kind of detail work that prevents leaks for decades. No shortcuts.

photos.alt: Clean metal valley flashing with new architectural shingles on both sides

projects.title: Two Properties — One Day
projects.description: Side-by-side tear-offs on neighboring properties. Full decking exposed, materials staged, crew running both roofs. Efficiency at scale — no wasted time.

photos.alt: Aerial drone shot of two roofs being replaced simultaneously
Top-down drone view of one roof stripped to bare decking with tear-off debris on tarps in the yard

projects.title: Apartment Complex — Tear-Off & Re-Roof
projects.description: Every roof on a multi-building apartment complex needed replacing. The crew tore each building off down to the decking and laid new synthetic underlayment, then finished every building in architectural shingles with new ridge vents and all flashing replaced. Drone-documented start to finish for the property management company; the range covers the whole complex.

photos.alt: Aerial drone view of apartment building mid-tearoff with blue underlayment and crew working
Complex-wide aerial mid tear-off with old shingles stripped and blue underlayment going down
Drone view of one building wrapped in blue synthetic underlayment with shingle bundles staged along the slope
Aerial drone view of completed multi-building apartment complex with new roofs
Completed new gray shingle roof on one building of the apartment complex at dusk

projects.title: A-Frame Cabin — Standing Seam Metal
projects.description: Not every job is shingles. This mountain A-frame got a standing seam metal roof — built for steep pitch, heavy snow loads, and decades of zero maintenance.

photos.alt: Three-quarter aerial of the A-frame cabin with the full sweep of its ribbed metal roof running down to the eave
Straight-on view of the A-frame front gable, the metal roof running symmetrically to both eaves
Close view of the metal roof field with the panel ribs running eave to ridge
Looking out from above the cabin across the wooded hillside setting
Directly overhead view of the A-frame cabin’s completed standing seam metal roof
Aerial view of the cabin community on the misty mountainside, metal roofs among the bare trees

projects.title: Seamless Gutters + Screens for Tree Cover
projects.description: New 5-inch seamless aluminum with fascia wood included — and screens sized run-by-run: the tree-covered runs got protection, the open runs did not get padded onto the bill.

photos.alt: New seamless gutter with mesh screens running the full eave of a home surrounded by woods, seen from the roof
Close-up along the new gutter screens installed tight to the shingle edge beneath overhanging tree branches
Two-story brick and siding home mid-installation with ladders set and the old gutter removed above the garage

projects.title: Three Layers Off — Full Tear-Off Re-Roof
projects.description: Three layers of old three-tab came off this Cincinnati two-story, and both old dormers came off with them. New GAF Timberline system on the slopes, chimneys re-flashed with new crickets, the built-in box gutters relined, and the flat sections sealed under a fresh aluminum coating. The whole job, documented start to finish.

photos.alt: Drone view of the crew stripping two layers of shingles down to plank decking on a two-story hip roof
Top-down view of exposed plank roof decking and the dormer opening beside remaining old shingles and a brick chimney
Freshly silver-coated flat roof section in front of the new architectural shingle slope and brick chimney
Wide drone view of the crew stripping the hip roof to plank decking, old shingles piling at the eaves
Angled overhead view of the stripped slopes, dormer opening, and the chimney rebuilt between fresh wood forms
The bare low-slope roof section from above the rake, prepped before its new aluminum coating
Drone overhead of the shingle field mid-strip with torn debris along the eaves and decking opening up at the ridge
Half-stripped roof from above: original plank decking exposed beside the brick chimney with crew working
Whole-house top-down view with the front slope stripped to plank decking and the rear slope still shingled
Fresh silver coating going down over the primed low-slope membrane, seen from behind the working roofer
The whole deck dried in under synthetic underlayment with the chimney prepped and shingle bundles staged
Straight-down view of the whole deck under synthetic underlayment with shingle bundles staged across it
A roofer nailing off beside the brick chimney as the new shingle courses reach it
A roofer sealing the new flashing at the tall brick chimney on the freshly shingled hip roof
Straight-down aerial with roughly two thirds of the new slate-blend architectural shingle laid
The steep-to-low-slope transition with fresh silver reflective coating over the flat section
The relined built-in box gutter running along the edge of the new shingles
Top-down on the tall brick chimney with its new step and counter flashing complete
New black step and counter flashing worked into the brick chimney beside the new shingles
Straight-down view of the completed roof, the full hip-and-valley field finished in new shingle
Overhead of the finished roof: the new shingle field, the relined box gutters and the silver-coated low-slope section at the front

projects.title: Thermal Scan → Ventilation Overhaul
projects.description: The thermal camera found the damp rafter bays before we opened anything up. Then the fix: upgraded with Roofivent — seven new units, Roto turbines and Eco vents, plus new pipe boots — and the bath fan finally vented outside where it belongs. Moisture problems you can see are moisture problems you can solve.

photos.alt: Overhead drone view of a gray shingle roof with seven new low-profile vents and turbines installed, large fenced backyard below
Thermal camera image of attic rafter bays glowing yellow and orange, with the temperature color scale on the right
Close-up of two new black Roofivent vents installed on the fresh shingle slope
New Roofivent low-profile vents and the vent elbow beside the repainted chimney with its new caps
New pipe boots and vents along the freshly shingled slope, with the repainted chimney and its new caps behind
Inside the attic: rafter bays over fresh blown-in insulation after the ventilation fix
Second thermal camera frame of a roof vent base and pipes, cool roof plane against the warmer attic below
Work-day close-up of a new Roofivent turbine freshly flashed in beside the old vent cap just removed
Wide aerial of the finished roof with the new vents down both slopes and fresh shingle patches at every penetration
View down the ridge line showing the new Roofivent units, blacked-out gooseneck and plumbing stacks by the chimney

projects.title: Storm-Torn Gable — Siding Restored
projects.description: Wind ripped this gable open two-and-a-half stories up — siding gone, the foam sheathing behind it punctured, gutter bent. We wrapped it fresh, worked in new panels to match, and straightened the gutter line. Storm damage doesn't always mean a whole new wall — sometimes it just needs someone willing to climb.

photos.alt: Three extension ladders set against the tall gable while a crew member installs new vinyl siding over fresh house wrap
The wind damage up close: torn siding, punctured foam sheathing, and a bent gutter above the porch roof
The damaged band stripped of siding panels — house wrap and brick exposed across the gable while the new panels wait below
Overhead drone view of the home's gray shingle roof and white flat-roof section on inspection day
Crew member on an extension ladder fitting a replacement siding panel high on the gable
Storm-torn vinyl siding panel ripped open and hanging off the wall
Impact hole punched clean through the siding and foam sheathing with insulation showing
Panel removed to reveal the punctured foam sheathing board behind the damaged siding
Three ladders on the stripped wall band with new siding panels staged and a crew member climbing
Installer nailing a new siding course over the fresh house wrap patch
The nearly finished wall with the installer on the ladder working the final courses

projects.title: Forty-Five Squares, Two Days
projects.description: Forty-five squares on an 8/12 pitch, and the old three-tab was streaked across every plane. Full tear-off, then Owens Corning Duration over synthetic underlayment — with ice-and-water at the eaves and valleys, and both skylights re-flashed at no extra charge because that is where these roofs leak. Two days, start to finish.

photos.alt: Drone view at eave height of the brick ranch before work, its old dark three-tab roof weathered and streaked
Straight-down aerial of the whole roof before tear-off, showing the hips, valleys, octagonal bay and two skylights
Aerial of the roof stripped clean to bare decking with shingle bundles staged on the driveway below
Tight view down the ridge to the brick chimney with the decking fully exposed and old step flashing still in place
Two roofers stripping shingles around the pair of skylights with the decking opened up beside them
Synthetic underlayment and ice-and-water membrane down over the octagonal bay with both skylights re-set and ready to flash
Roofer nailing hip cap where the new architectural shingle field meets the last strip of underlayment beside the chimney
Straight-down aerial with the new shingle field laid across the main roof and only the far wing still on underlayment
Wide view of the rear elevation on its wooded hillside with the new roof on, walkout level and deck below

projects.title: Wind Took the Roof — Tarped That Day
projects.description: March wind stripped the low-slope section down to felt and nails. We inspected it the same day and got a tarp down before the next rain — then documented it for the claim and met the adjuster, through to a full replacement. The emergency call is the part insurance forgets to tell you about; these photos are that day.

photos.alt: Wind-stripped low-slope roof section with the mineral-surfaced roll roofing peeled back in a large ragged sheet
A section of roll roofing torn clean away, bounded on both sides by intact granulated surface
Close view of the torn edge with exposed felt, scattered backed-out nails and the decking board lines showing through
Crew member on the ridge lifting away a storm-loosened ridge cap shingle
Crew member fastening the blue emergency tarp along the ridge with orange cap nails
The finished emergency dry-in: the blue tarp laid over the stripped section and buttoned down with a grid of cap nails

projects.title: Open Top Course — Newport Fix
projects.description: The top course of siding was gone along the whole run at the head of a two-story wall — a straight opening into the wall cavity. Ladder up, piece back in, seated tight under the trim. Same-day, three hundred and fifty dollars, and no one had to climb it twice.

photos.alt: The top course of vinyl siding missing along the run at the head of a two-story wall, leaving the cavity open
Looking up the extension ladder at the open course with the worker seen from behind
The full ladder run from the ground as the replacement piece goes back into the course
Low angle up the red extension ladder to the worker at the top course, a tree beside the wall
The worker at the top of the extension ladder, working along the head of the tan vinyl wall
From under an overhang, the full height of the wall: the ladder runs from the brick base past the windows to the worker at the top
The finished wall with the run closed, no ladder and nobody in frame
Close view of the head of the wall with the top course back in and seated tight under the trim board

projects.title: Two Broken Soffit Boards
projects.description: Two broken boards in the overhang of a stucco two-story, in two separate spots. Replacement boards cut and painted on the ground first, roof protection down before the ladders went up, then both areas closed back in. Small job, done like a big one.

photos.alt: Cream stucco two-story shot from the ground, the damaged overhang visible at the roof line
Close view of the overhang where the broken soffit boards left the framing exposed
Replacement boards laid out on a drop cloth and painted before installation
Extension ladder set against the house with roof protection down before the repair
The same corner of the overhang repaired, new boards in and painted to match

projects.title: Rot Filled, Sanded, Painted to Blend
projects.description: Painted wood lap siding with rot breaches open at two separate spots — the kind of thing that quietly lets water into a wall for years. Every cavity packed with exterior filler, sanded flush, and painted to blend. You have to know where it was to see it.

photos.alt: Close-up of two rotted-through breaches in the painted wood lap siding hard against the white corner board
A second damage site beside the window trim, one breach ringed by a crumbling earlier patch that had let go
Exterior wood filler packed into the cavity and sanded flush with the board profile
The finished repair painted to blend, brush texture feathered into the lap and up to the corner board
Golden-hour view of the two-story yellow lap-siding elevation with the repaired corner and the downspout strapped full height

projects.title: One Shake, Back Where It Belongs
projects.description: A single fiber-cement shake had let go of the front gable. We cleaned the failed adhesive off both surfaces, prepped them properly, and set the original piece back so the field runs continuous again. Two hundred and fifty dollars — because that is what it was worth.

photos.alt: Front gable fiber-cement shake field with one shake missing, the bare patch and old adhesive residue visible mid-field
Extension ladder set against the front gable, looking up the elevation
Tight frame on the reattached shake with its fastener heads set flush
The same front gable with the shake field continuous again and the reattached piece sitting flush and on-course

projects.title: Color-Matched Wind Repair
projects.description: Wind damage on a brick ranch — an insurance job. The part worth looking at is the blend: new shingles woven into the existing field so the repair does not announce itself from the driveway. Matching an aged roof is most of the skill in a repair.

photos.alt: Wide view across the main roof plane in late-afternoon light with the repair area under way
Chest-camera view down onto the hip as new shingles are woven into the existing courses
Tight detail of the shingle field where new and existing shingles meet
The finished repair blending into the surrounding field up to the ridge
Ground-level view of the finished brick ranch in evening light with the repaired roof in place

projects.title: House, Garage and Outbuilding
projects.description: Worn, curling three-tab with patch repairs already layered on it — on the ranch, the attached garage, and the detached outbuilding out back. All three came off and went back new, finished in one late-December push with the light going.

photos.alt: Drone view of the original roof: worn, curling three-tab with several mismatched lighter patch repairs
Straight-down view of the failing three-tab field showing granule loss, staining and at least three patch-repair blocks
Working shot with the new roof mostly laid, dump trailer backed to the garage and heaped with tear-off
Whole-property view from above: house and attached garage finished in new laminate shingle, the detached outbuilding under way
Close crop of the finished ridge line with new ridge vent and re-flashed chimney
Front elevation of the completed roof across the house and attached garage, shot from the driveway

projects.title: Sixty-Eight Feet of Ridge
projects.description: About sixty-eight feet of old aluminum ridge vent came off this gambrel building, running the full length of the original structure and the addition. Closed back in and capped end to end with shingle. A long, straight, boring ridge line — which is exactly what you want.

photos.alt: Ground-level end elevation of the gambrel-roofed building on evaluation day
Wide aerial of the full structure at the start of the job with materials staged
Tight aerial straight down the ridge with the old aluminum vent removed and the ridge opened up
Close-up of the finished shingle ridge cap running end to end with sealant dabs along both slopes
Oblique aerial of the completed building with the ridge capped end to end and no aluminum vent remaining

projects.title: Three Roof Systems, One Victorian
projects.description: Three stories, three different roof systems, and a chimney base patched with tar by somebody before us. Full tear-off, then architectural shingle on the steep mansard, EPDM on the flat, and five dormer caps converted from rubber to shingle. These photos are what we found going in.

photos.alt: Three-story white Victorian with a steep mansard, dormers and a flat upper roof, shot from the front
Straight-down view showing all three roof systems in one frame: shingle mansard, flat membrane and dormer caps
Angled view of the third-story flat roof with aging membrane, visible seams and patches, and the brick chimney rising off it
A dormer bay capped in rubber membrane rather than shingle, the condition the job converted back to shingle
Close view of the steep mansard with granule-worn three-tab shingles and a mismatched patch repair mid-field
Top-down view of a bay cap where a rubber membrane panel sits in the surrounding aged shingle field, edges sealed with mastic
The brick chimney base on the flat roof buried under layers of troweled tar and sealant from prior repairs
Aerial over the rear of the three-story house before the work, aged dark-green shingles on the mansard and the failing flat above
Install day on the mansard with the crew running new pewter-grey architectural shingles up the hip
Straight-down view of the finished third-story flat roof with the new membrane fully adhered and both chimneys re-flashed
Close view of the transition itself: new membrane on one side, new pewter-grey shingle on the other, joined with fresh edge metal
The completed roof from a matching angle to the before frame, all three systems finished in one shot

projects.title: Ten-Twelve Pitch, Plank Decking
projects.description: Fourteen squares across seven facets at a 10/12 pitch — steep enough that everything takes longer and costs more to do safely. Stripped to the original one-by plank decking, then GAF Timberline HDZ over premium synthetic. Nothing exotic, just done right on a hard roof.

photos.alt: Top-down view of the original roof: weathered, streaked shingles across all seven facets with the masonry chimney mid-slope
Angled aerial down the long slope showing how steep the 10/12 pitch is, with the valley, chimney and dormer gable in frame
Top-down view after tear-off with the roof stripped to bare plank sheathing and old shingles piled on tarps below
Tight aerial down the ridge showing the old one-by plank decking board by board, including the gaps and deteriorated boards
A roofer working the bare deck with a tear-off shovel, dump trailer loaded and tarps protecting the beds and AC unit
Three crew working the stripped deck around the masonry chimney ahead of the re-flash

projects.title: House and Outbuildings, One Day
projects.description: The carrier approved part of this claim and denied the rest, which is where most homeowners give up. We worked the rest of it, then did the job: house and outbuildings stripped and dried in by morning, charcoal GAF Timberline HDZ across the whole roof by mid-afternoon.

photos.alt: Tear-off in progress on an outbuilding with the failed old green three-tab shingles coming off
The whole house stripped to deck and dried in at eight in the morning, with new shingle bundles staged across the roof
Aerial over the finished house the same afternoon with new charcoal architectural shingles across the full roof
Close view of the finished shingle field around the replaced furnace vent and its new storm collar

projects.title: Three Layers Off a Half-Timbered Tudor
projects.description: Three layers came off this half-timbered Tudor — the biggest tear-off on this page. Wind damage started the claim, and the roof that went back on has to sit right against a house with that much character. Sprawling cruciform footprint, multiple chimneys, dormers into shingle-sided walls.

photos.alt: Top-down drone view of the finished roof across the whole cruciform footprint in new multi-tone shingle
Oblique aerial of the finished roof plane and chimneys, set against a neighbouring weathered grey roof
Close detail of new shingles running into a green-trimmed, shingle-sided dormer beside the chimney
Dusk aerial of the whole house, the new roof reading pale against deep summer tree canopy

projects.title: Down to the Rafters
projects.description: Sometimes the decking underneath is the actual problem. This one came off entirely — open rafters, daylight through the roof — then went back with new sheathing before a single shingle was laid. You only get to do this part once, so it is worth seeing.

photos.alt: Decking fully stripped with bare rafters and gusset plates open straight to daylight
The same slope re-sheathed in clean new decking with chalk lines snapped, ready for underlayment
The finished roof looking up the ridge line in warm multi-tone dimensional shingle with new vents and pipe boot
The finished slope showing the full vent layout with five new metal vents, pipe boot and exhaust cap

projects.title: Two Layers, and the Landscaping Survived
projects.description: Two layers of asphalt off a white ranch, down to the original plank decking with old tar still stuck to the boards. The part worth pointing at is the ground: beds tarped, plants covered, nothing trampled. A tear-off makes a mess — leaving one behind is a choice.

photos.alt: The ranch mid tear-off, stripped to bare plank deck with ladders up and the landscaping beds tarped below
Close view of the exposed original plank decking with torn asphalt and old tar still stuck to the boards
The finished roof from the ridge in full sun, new grey shingles running the length of the house past the brick chimney

projects.title: Charcoal Over the River Valley
projects.description: A smaller insurance job on a hillside lot, done properly and handed back clean. Stripped to the deck, then charcoal dimensional shingle with tight even courses. The view off the back is the bonus.

photos.alt: The deck stripped to bare sheathing and scattered with torn-off asphalt, hillside back yard below
The finished charcoal roof looking down the ridge with the wooded river valley opening up behind
The finished hip in charcoal dimensional shingle with tight even courses and a new gutter line

projects.title: Hail and Wind — Chimney Done Right
projects.description: Hail and wind insurance job, start to finish. Deck stripped and dried in under synthetic with new drip edge, then a light grey field over the whole house. Look at the corbelled brick chimney — new step flashing worked up every course, which is the part that leaks when somebody rushes it.

photos.alt: The deck stripped and dried in with synthetic underlayment run out over the full slope and new drip edge on
Crew laying underlayment with the ridge still open, the original ridge board and old decking visible
New black step flashing stepped cleanly up the corbelled brick chimney against the finished light grey field
The long finished slope running down toward the street with the chimney and ridge at the head of the frame
The finished plane from the opposite side with a new vent set in the field and the chimney at right

projects.title: Three Generations of Decking
projects.description: Strip this brick ranch and you find the whole history of it: original plank, a stretch of older plywood, and the new sheathing we put down. Open rafter bays, landscaping tarped, materials staged. This is what the middle of a storm job actually looks like.

photos.alt: Straight-down view of the entire roof stripped to bare deck, a patchwork of old plank, plywood and fresh sheathing
Oblique aerial of the brick ranch with its rear slope opened to the rafters
Full-property view showing the stripped deck, open rafter bays, tarped landscaping and staged materials
A new galvanised vent stack and flashed base set on cleaned deck beside a fresh sheet of decking
Close decking detail with three generations of substrate side by side: original plank, older plywood and new sheathing
Eave-level view of the stripped edge where the old nail-riddled plank deck meets the existing trim

projects.title: A Second Opinion, For $140
projects.description: Somebody told this homeowner what her roof needed. She wanted a second read before spending real money, so she paid me a hundred and forty dollars to go look and write it up honestly. Missing drip edge, rot at the window head, an exposed deck edge over the gutter. Sometimes the most useful thing I sell is an answer.

photos.alt: Looking up under the rake edge where the shingle course overhangs a weathered unpainted fascia board with no drip edge
Rotted, delaminating wood trim at a window head on cedar siding, the paint peeled back to bare wood
Soffit underside with the raw deck edge left exposed above the gutter where the sub-fascia should close it in
Upward view along the gutter line into the downspout elbow at the gable corner

projects.title: Plank Deck to Finished, Seven Hours
projects.description: Stripped to the original board sheathing in the morning, finished grey laminate with crisp hip and ridge lines by late afternoon. The overhead pair tells it best — same framing, seven hours apart.

photos.alt: Oblique aerial with the entire hip roof stripped to its original board sheathing, bare planks running the full field
Straight-down view of the same deck where the plank courses and a new sheathing section split the frame
The finished roof seven hours later in grey architectural laminate with crisp hip and ridge cap lines
Straight-down view of the completed roof, framed to match the bare-deck shot for a direct comparison

projects.title: Bare Deck at Dawn, Done by Dark
projects.description: Tear-off complete across every plane, ground fully tarped, debris truck loaded — then synthetic underlayment over the whole field and a finished grey roof the same afternoon. Gutters back on before we left.

photos.alt: Tear-off complete with the roof down to bare sheathing across every plane, ground fully tarped and the debris truck loaded
The full field covered in synthetic underlayment with new drip edge run out along the eaves
The finished roof the same afternoon with an even grey laminate field, clean ridge line and rake edges
Straight-down view of the completed roof, framed to match the bare-deck shot

projects.title: One-Piece Siding Fix + Whole-Roof Walk & Caulk
projects.description: A gable-peak joint had opened up where the J-channel meets the trim — one-piece siding repair, sealed back tight. While we were up there we walked the whole roof and hit every exposed fastener and flashing seam with sealant. Small job, treated like a big one.

photos.alt: Close-up before photo at a gable peak: a gloved hand points to an open gap where the painted fascia trim and J-channel meet above vinyl siding
Work-in-progress close-up of the gable peak joint with black sealant worked into the gap between the fascia trim and the J-channel
After photo of the gable peak with the J-channel and painted trim sitting tight against the vinyl siding, the joint resealed with no visible gap
Roof detail of a shingle patch between two metal flashing runs, with fresh sealant along the shingle seam
Detail of a metal flashing seam on an asphalt shingle roof, with an exposed fastener head capped under a dab of black sealant

projects.title: Wind-Lifted Shingles, Reset by Hand
projects.description: Wind tore tabs loose across one slope and some shingles came apart in two layers when handled. We documented everything for the claim, backed the nails out with a shingle ripper, and reset the courses by hand — replacing what was too far gone.

photos.alt: Looking down a gray asphalt shingle roof at a long strip of wind-torn, missing shingles beside the exposed area during inspection
Close-up of a roofer’s hand pointing to missing shingle tabs and exposed dark underlayment on a wind-damaged asphalt roof
Two roofing technicians examine a delaminated shingle tab lifted from the roof, showing the torn edge left by wind damage
Hammer and nail-puller pry bar laid on the shingles as a technician lifts the edge of a wind-damaged shingle to begin replacement
Technician uses a nail puller to extract fasteners from beneath a lifted shingle, with pulled roofing nails lying on the shingles nearby
Wide view of the roof plane as a technician fits fresh replacement shingles into the wind-damaged section

projects.title: Rain-Day Flat Roof Inspection
projects.description: You inspect a flat roof right after the rain, because that is when it shows itself. We walked this EPDM roof in the wet — mapped the ponding, an un-taped lap seam, a torn corner at the drain, and what was still holding — and delivered a 13-photo written report.

photos.alt: Standing water across a flat EPDM roof after rain, with twigs and leaf debris pinned in the ponding and an inspector’s boot at the water’s edge for scale
Close-up of a horizontal EPDM lap seam without cover tape, the membrane edge lifting slightly above the rain-wet field
Fingertip pointing to torn, bunched EPDM membrane at a corner drain fitting on a flat roof edge, where the sheet should lap flat and sealed
Rubber pipe boot flashing sealed tight around a cast-iron plumbing vent penetration on an EPDM roof, ringed by standing water after rain
Metal step flashing bedded in a continuous sealant bead where a flat EPDM roof meets brick masonry, photographed wet after rain

projects.title: By Golly’s: Emergency Calls to Full Rebuild
projects.description: By Golly’s Bar & Grill in Milford had active leaks after wind damage: four emergency calls including a same-day tarp to keep the kitchen open, then the real fix — 32 squares of old rubber roof torn off, new insulation board down, 60-mil EPDM over the whole low-slope section, with the rooftop HVAC craned off and reset to do it right.

photos.alt: Crew tearing off a commercial low-slope roof, with the old EPDM membrane peeled back over water-stained recovery board and rotted layers exposed beside new parapet framing

Exposed roof deck during an EPDM tear-off beside a rooftop exhaust unit, showing weathered wood-fiber board and rusted fastener plates as the crew re-fastens the deck before new insulation and membrane go down

projects.title: Warranty-Claim Shingle Samples, Pulled Right
projects.description: The shingle manufacturer’s claims department needed samples pulled a specific way, in a specific condition. We made the site visit, documented the leak area, pulled the samples per spec, sealed every removal spot with a temporary weather-tight patch, and left the homeowner a written field summary for their claim file.

photos.alt: Full strip of aged three-tab asphalt shingle laid on a concrete walkway after removal from the roof, showing heavy granule loss, a worn seam line, and torn spots along one edge
A roofer’s hand lifts the corner of an unsealed asphalt shingle tab to show the unbonded underside and trapped debris, the other hand holding a stick of white marking chalk
White chalk arrow drawn on a gray asphalt shingle roof pointing to a spot of granule loss and surface damage marked for warranty documentation
Removed asphalt shingle sample strips laid flat on gray-painted porch decking against the home’s light siding, staged for warranty-claim documentation

projects.title: Barn-Style Shed, Down to the OSB
projects.description: Barn-style backyard shed in Mason — old rolled roofing, torn off completely rather than covered over. With it off we could actually look at the deck: original OSB with old asphalt still stuck to it, sound underneath. Then synthetic underlayment, charcoal architectural shingles and a shingle ridge cap. Same shingle that goes on a house.

photos.alt: White gambrel shed with dark green trim and double doors under a new charcoal shingle roof, chain-link fence and woods behind
Worker on a gambrel shed roof tearing black rolled roofing off, bare OSB decking exposed and green-trimmed gable below
Close-up of bare OSB roof decking with old black asphalt residue stuck to the strands and torn roll roofing at the right edge
Shed mid-job with new charcoal shingles on the lower slope, a blue tarp over the unfinished upper roof, and torn-off roll roofing on the grass
New charcoal architectural shingles run up the shed's roof slope, blue synthetic underlayment still exposed along the top edge
New charcoal shingles and ridge cap on the shed's gambrel slope, ladders leaning against the white siding, old black roofing piled below

projects.title: Gutter Section & Shingle Repair
projects.description: Replaced a damaged gutter section and tied it back into the existing downspout, then repaired storm-loosened shingles on the roof, matching the field as closely as the existing shingle allowed.

photos.alt: Aerial view of a shingle roof between two neighboring houses, showing the ridge, chimney vent, and dormer window
Ground-level view of a new white gutter and downspout running down the corner of a blue-sided house
Overhead view of a repaired section of architectural shingles, color-matched against the surrounding roof field

projects.title: LP SmartSide Trim & Corner Repair
projects.description: Replaced woodpecker-damaged and rotted corner trim and door-surround boards on LP SmartSide siding, primed and painted to match, with a roof walk to catch and seal exposed fasteners along the way.

photos.alt: Joe kneeling on a roof edge removing a damaged corner trim board with a pry tool
Wide view of a gable end with LP SmartSide siding, corner trim board opened up mid-repair to expose the substrate beneath
Removed length of rotted wood trim laid on the grass, showing split and decayed wood along its length

projects.title: Ceiling & Wall Crack Repair
projects.description: Filled and finished cracks, gaps and separated joints across a full ceiling and walls, re-taped and re-mudded where the old tape had lifted, caulked and sanded smooth — left ready for the homeowner's own paint.

photos.alt: Hairline crack running across a garage ceiling near a fluorescent light fixture
Crack along a ceiling-to-wall corner seam above a window
Freshly re-mudded ceiling and wall joint, patched and feathered smooth ahead of paint

projects.title: Storm Siding Refasten + Gutter Repair
projects.description: Wind pulled the siding fasteners loose across several courses — we unlocked, refastened and re-locked the wall so it lies flat with no bubbles, plus a matching aluminum gutter extension carried the downspout the rest of the way to the ground.

photos.alt: Two-story home with navy board-and-batten gable and blue vinyl siding, repaired wall lying flat
Rooftop view of a new gutter corner and downspout at the eave, overlooking the neighborhood street
Close-up of a gutter corner miter and downspout outlet against gray vinyl siding

projects.title: 122 Ft. of New Gutters + Micromesh Screens
projects.description: 122 linear feet of new 5-inch seamless aluminum gutter across a full two-story run, capped end to end with micromesh leaf screens — no exposed seams, no gaps at the corners.

photos.alt: Ladder set against a second roofline showing the micromesh screen running the gutter edge, trees in the background
Close-up of a micromesh gutter screen panel held up next to a sample of black mesh guard

projects.title: Tongue-and-Groove Soffit Repair Near the Roofline
projects.description: A gap in the tongue-and-groove soffit seam had opened up at the roofline, exposing the cavity underneath — closed back in and resealed so the gable line reads clean again.

photos.alt: Open soffit cavity at a roofline corner showing the sheathing and framing before repair
Cut tongue-and-groove soffit boards and hand tools laid out on a drop cloth ready for installation
Gable roofline exterior with the soffit line closed and resealed after the repair

projects.title: Same-Day Gutter Cleaning, Cleared by Hand
projects.description: A clogged downspout and packed leaf debris cleared by hand across every run, then flush-tested to confirm free flow — same-day service, no shortcuts.

photos.alt: Gloved hand clearing packed leaf debris out of a gutter run by hand, mesh guard lifted for access
Downspout opening packed with dark decomposed leaf debris before cleaning
Clean shingle roofline with a clear gutter and mesh screen after the cleaning was completed

projects.title: Downspout Base Connector Replaced & Reconnected
projects.description: The base section of a downspout had failed where it met the underground drain line — replaced with a new connector, tied back into the existing PVC line, and painted to match.

photos.alt: Close-up of a new black downspout base connector fitted where the downspout meets the foundation
Downspout base connector tied into the underground drain line at the foundation of a brick home
